ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7); no account flag against the driver.
ruling.reasoning:
The fee at issue is the $6.61 no-show cancellation fee, charged by the driver against a rider who says she came out a minute after the cancellation [F4][F7]. NS-0 routes the case: cancelled_by = driver with a no-show claim, so it is decided under NS-1 and NS-2, and the RydeX fixed-fare model means the only disputed item is the cancellation fee itself [F4][NS-0].

NS-1(i) and (ii) are satisfied: the driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 13:02:35 (a driver tap, not a platform auto-confirmation), and the GPS put him 39 m from the pickup at that moment, inside the 200 m radius [F6][F1][NS-1].

NS-1(iii) fails. The policy counts only the continuous period within the pickup radius after the tap, and the system measure is 175 s (2 min 55 s) after the 13:02:35 tap, against a required >180 s (at least 3:01) [F6][NS-1]. The longer figures in the record do not rescue the driver: the 4 min 30 s cumulative within 200 m [F2] and the 3 min 15 s stationary period 40 m away [F3] both began before the tap (13:01:00 and 13:02:15 respectively), and NS-1 expressly excludes pre-tap time from (iii) [F3][F6][NS-1]. The platform-recorded arrival at 13:01:00 and the 4 min 30 s to cancellation [F5] are likewise not the NS-1 measure, which runs from the arrival confirmation [F5][F6][NS-1]. The driver's post-trip statement that he waited more than 3 minutes [F12] and his chat line 'More than 3 min already' [F10] are statements, and the system record [F6] governs them [F10][F12][NS-1]. No record in the file sets a longer no-show threshold for this case, so the NS-1 default of more than 3 minutes applies [F6][NS-1].

Because NS-1 (iii) is not met, NS-2 gives the rider a full refund of the $6.61 cancellation fee [F4][F7][NS-2]. As a RydeX fixed-fare trip there is no metered mileage component and no surge to adjust [F8][NS-0][NS-2].

The NS-2 flag condition is not triggered: it attaches only where the arrival confirmation was made while the GPS showed the driver outside the 200 m radius, and the record shows 39 m at the tap [F6][F1][NS-2]. The rider's request to flag under RD-6 also fails, because RD-6 requires an established route-deviation case (an RD-2 refund above zero or a recorded RD-1 breach), and this is a no-show case with no deviation segment [F4][NS-0][RD-6]. The driver's profile - 2 disputes, 1 upheld (no-show) in 90 days - is a profile fact and cannot decide anything on its own [F17][RD-6].

On safety, I read both chat messages [F9][F10], the driver's statement [F12] and the complaint: 'Reached, blue Toyota Prius, waiting at the pickup', 'More than 3 min already, I have to cancel' and the rider's assertion of lateness. There is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation in any of them [F9][F10][F12][SAFE-1]. Evidence is sufficient: the timeline covers arrival to cancellation without a GPS hole [F2][F6], the chat is complete and every message is timestamped [F11], and no compensation element depends on a missing record [F6][NS-1].

rejected_claims.reason: Withdrawn by the driver advocate and contradicted by the system record: NS-1(iii) counts only the continuous period after the 'I'm Here' tap, and that period is 175 s (2 min 55 s), below the required >180 s; the stationary time from 13:02:15 [F3] and the closest approach of 38 m [F1] do not change a post-tap measurement [F6][NS-1].

Withdrawn by the driver advocate and wrong on the clause: a no-show cancellation fee stands only if NS-1 is satisfied in full, and (iii) fails on the post-tap measure of 175 s [F6], so the $6.61 must be refunded under NS-2 [F4][F7][NS-1][NS-2].
Withdrawn and in any case immaterial: the rider's clean 90-day profile [F16] cannot decide a no-show case either way; the finding rests on the system measurement in F6 [F6][F16][NS-1].

RD-6 is a route-deviation clause and applies only where an RD-2 refund exceeds zero or an RD-1 breach is recorded; this is a no-show case with no off-route segment [F4][NS-0][RD-6]. The NS-2 flag attaches only where the arrival confirmation occurred outside the 200 m radius, and the record shows 39 m at the tap [F6][F1][NS-2]. A prior upheld dispute in the driver's 90-day profile [F17] is a profile fact and cannot by itself create a repeat finding [F17][RD-6].

Accepted only as immaterial: the rider's 0 disputes / 0 upheld in 90 days [F16] is a profile fact that cannot decide the no-show question; the ruling rests on the NS-1 (iii) measurement in F6 [F16][F6][NS-1].

what_would_change: Had NS-1 (iii) held ((iii) stayed at the pickup more than 3 min after the arrival confirmation, until cancelling (NS-1 default: more than 3 min)), the fee would stand and no refund would be due.
